cards.explanation: The answer is restore him. Paul says, "…you who are spiritual should restore him with a spirit of gentleness." Notice he doesn't say to hand the person a lecture and a clipboard, friends. Restoring means helping him back up, and Paul points the spiritual ones toward that (Galatians 6:1).

The answer is True. Paul says to restore him "…with a spirit of gentleness." (Galatians 6:1). Gentleness is how it's done, friends. Think of how you'd handle a fresh batch of cookies straight out of the oven: slow hands and no slamming.

The answer is tempted. Paul says, "But watch yourself, or you also may be tempted." (Galatians 6:1). The one doing the helping isn't above temptation himself. I'll admit that keeps me humble, friends, because I'm the guy who needs a reminder every time.

The answer is the law of Christ. Paul says, "Carry one another’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ." (Galatians 6:2). Carrying each other's weight isn't extra credit, friends. Paul ties it right to Christ's own law.

The answer is himself. Paul says, "If anyone thinks he is something when he is nothing, he deceives himself." (Galatians 6:3). Nobody else even had to be fooled, friends. He did the whole job on his own, like a guy who bakes one batch and sits there convinced he's the best in town.

The answer is False. Paul says the one who tests his own work "…will have reason to boast in himself alone, and not in someone else." (Galatians 6:4). So no riding on a neighbor's batch, friends. Your own work has to stand up on its own.

The answer is his own load. Paul says, "For each one should carry his own load." (Galatians 6:5). Two thoughts sit side by side here, friends: carrying each other's burdens and carrying your own load. Paul keeps both in the same breath.

The answer is all good things. Paul says the one who receives instruction "…must share in all good things with his instructor." (Galatians 6:6). Notice he says all good things, friends. He doesn't say a few crumbs off the edge of the tray.
The answer is sows. Paul says, "Whatever a man sows, he will reap in return." (Galatians 6:7). Sowing comes first and reaping comes after, friends. You get back what you planted.
The answer is eternal life. Paul says, "…the one who sows to please the Spirit, from the Spirit will reap eternal life." (Galatians 6:8). The Spirit is the source of that harvest, friends.

The answer is True. Paul says, "The one who sows to please his flesh, from the flesh will reap destruction…" (Galatians 6:8). It's a serious line, friends, and Paul sets it right beside the promise about the Spirit. Both ways of sowing get their own harvest.

The answer is harvest. Paul says, "Let us not grow weary in well-doing, for in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up." (Galatians 6:9). The harvest comes in due time, so keep going, friends. Even a good farmer doesn't dig up the seeds every morning to check on them.
The answer is False. Paul says, "…in due time we will reap a harvest if we do not give up." (Galatians 6:9). The "if" matters there, friends. Keep at it and don't give up.

The answer is the family of faith. Paul says, "…let us do good to everyone, and especially to the family of faith." (Galatians 6:10). Good to everyone, friends, with special care for the family of faith. I'm a stamper with six cookie cutter kids, so I know how family feels.
